q: 2026-10-11, why did it had the lowest sale
answer:
Short answer — 2026-10-11 was low because orders fell sharply: Net sales were ₹34,377 (−51% vs 2026-10-10) driven mainly by a 47% drop in orders; the system found no single upstream cause it could confirm. (Measured)

Evidence — key measured values (previous day → 2026-10-11)
- Net sales: ₹70,517 → ₹34,377 (Measured)
- Orders: 36 → 19 (Measured)
- Net AOV: ₹1,959 → ₹1,809 (Measured)
- Gross sales: ₹72,814 → ₹36,166 (Measured)
- Product P&L ad spend (allocated): ₹45,085 → ₹40,080 (Measured)
- Conversion rate: 0.66% → 0.58% (Measured)
- Sessions: 3,929 → 3,423 (Measured)

What changed (compact, Verified arithmetic)
- Exact split: Orders drop (−47%) explains ~100% of the net sales fall; Net AOV moved little (−8%) and contributed ~0% to the decline. (Derived — decomposition)
- Within orders, the conversion-rate fall (−41%) contributed ~82% of the orders drop; sessions fell −16%. (Measured → Derived)

What we did and the confidence
- The diagnosis decomposed net sales into gross sales, deductions and their parts and tested common upstream drivers (ad spend, impressions, clicks). No driver met the threshold to be labelled a supported cause — ad spend and impressions were within normal ranges and clicks/sessions did not move unusually. (Measured / Tested)

Period: 2026-10-10 vs 2026-10-11 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
